Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Section 17(b) gives us (Sparkling) an unqualified right to terminate for convenience at any time on ninety (90) days' written notice, and no early-termination fee or penalty is imposed anywhere (Section 11 and the Fee Schedule reference no exit charge). Garman has no corresponding convenience right: its only termination rights arise under Section 17(c) on insolvency or uncured material default, which satisfies the preferred position that the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term. The clause therefore sits at the fallback on notice period (60–90 days rather than the preferred 30 days) and better than fallback on fees, so it is compliant and we do not redline it. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted only: the 90-day notice is at the outer edge of the fallback range, and Section 17(b) contains no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (refund of fees for services not yet rendered is expressly provided only on termination for Garman's default under Section 17(c)). If the agreement is reopened for other reasons, we would seek 30 days' notice and an express pro-rata refund.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Section 17(b) gives us (Sparkling) an unqualified right to terminate for convenience at any time on ninety (90) days' written notice, and no early-termination fee or penalty is imposed anywhere (Section 11 and the Fee Schedule reference no exit charge). Garman has no corresponding convenience right: its only termination rights arise under Section 17(c) on insolvency or uncured material default, which satisfies the preferred position that the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term. The clause therefore sits at the fallback on notice period (60–90 days rather than the preferred 30 days) and better than fallback on fees, so it is compliant and we do not redline it. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted only: the 90-day notice is at the outer edge of the fallback range, and Section 17(b) contains no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (refund of fees for services not yet rendered is expressly provided only on termination for Garman's default under Section 17(c)). If the agreement is reopened for other reasons, we would seek 30 days' notice and an express pro-rata refund.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from the supplied source. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change.

This is a bounded short-document repair and you have no tools. The user supplies the exact source paragraphs, definitions, current proposal, and deterministic feedback. Return only the requested structured proposal and one-to-one element coverage. Copy every replace.oldText byte-for-byte from a supplied paragraph. Do not invent an anchor or source text.

- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

input.quote: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages ... input.rationale: Section 15 is the only liability provision in the Agreement (Sections 11–14 contain no cap or aggregate liability language). It mutually excludes indirect and consequential damages and disapplies its limitations to Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality), but it contains no monetary cap of any kind, so each party — including Sparkling — bears unlimited exposure for direct damages. That fails the fallback, which requires a mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees. We therefore added the preferred mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000), kept the existing Section 13/14 carve-outs and extended them to indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmed that Sparkling's fee obligations are not capped "damages". The mutual exclusion of consequential damages already meets the preferred position and is left untouched.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

input.rationale: Section 15 is the only liability provision in the Agreement (Sections 11–14 contain no cap or aggregate liability language). It mutually excludes indirect and consequential damages and disapplies its limitations to Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality), but it contains no monetary cap of any kind, so each party — including Sparkling — bears unlimited exposure for direct damages. That fails the fallback, which requires a mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees. We therefore added the preferred mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000), kept the existing Section 13/14 carve-outs and extended them to indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmed that Sparkling's fee obligations are not capped "damages". The exclusion of consequential damages already meets the preferred position and is left untouched.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control

"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

**Finding: compliant (at fallback)** — Rule T4C, Termination for convenience.

- **Our exit right:** § 17(b) lets Sparkling terminate at any time on 90 days' written notice — within the fallback range (60–90 days), with no early-termination fee or penalty anywhere in the agreement (§ 11 / Fee Schedule impose none), which is better than the fallback's 3-month fee cap.
- **Vendor exit right:** Garman has no convenience right at all; its only termination triggers are insolvency events and uncured material default under § 17(c), meeting the preferred position.
- **Noted, not flagged:** notice sits at the outer edge of the fallback (90 vs. preferred 30 days), and § 17(b) has no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (refunds for services not yet rendered appear only on termination for Garman's default, p0128). These are sub-elements to raise if the agreement is reopened, not standalone deviations.

No redline proposed.

input.quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
input.rationale: There is no automatic-renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement. Maintenance runs for a "renewable one-year term" (p0065), i.e. renewal for a further 12 months requires the parties to agree and Sparkling to elect to pay the renewal maintenance fees; the licence itself is perpetual so long as fees are paid (p0117), and Sparkling may in any event exit on ninety (90) days' notice at any time (p0118). That matches the preferred position (renewal by mutual agreement, 12-month periods, no evergreen lock-in and no non-renewal notice window to compute), and it is more favourable to us than the fallback. The only preferred sub-element absent is an express cap on renewal-fee uplift (lesser of CPI and 3%) — the Fee Schedule contains no escalation language at all, so there is no unilateral uplift right for Garman to exercise; we note this rather than flagging it, and would seek a CPI/3% cap on renewal maintenance fees if the Fee Schedule is reopened.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

input.quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
input.rationale: There is no automatic-renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement. Maintenance runs for a "renewable one-year term" (p0065), i.e. renewal for a further 12 months requires the parties to agree and Sparkling to elect to pay the renewal maintenance fees; the licence itself is perpetual so long as fees are paid (p0117), and Sparkling may in any event exit on ninety (90) days' notice at any time (p0118). That matches the preferred position (renewal by mutual agreement, 12-month periods, no evergreen lock-in and no non-renewal notice window to compute), and it is more favourable to us than the fallback. The only preferred sub-element absent is an express cap on renewal-fee uplift (lesser of CPI and 3%) — the Fee Schedule contains no escalation language at all, so there is no unilateral uplift right for Garman to exercise; we note this rather than flagging it, and would seek a CPI/3% cap on renewal maintenance fees if the Fee Schedule is reopened.

paragraphs.text: 2. GRANT OF LICENSE

Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation. Sparkling's right, if any, to use the Software and Documentation at locations other than the Authorized Locations is subject to the payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule.
3. RESTRICTIONS ON USE
Sparkling shall:
(a) not copy the Software except to copy it onto another AS400 at the Authorized Locations and to make copies of the Software at each Authorized Location solely for backup purposes;
(b) not copy any of the Documentation except as required for Sparkling's internal purposes related to Sparkling's use of the Software;
(c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
(d) not reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble the Software;
(e) not use the Work except as authorized herein;
(f) take all reasonable precautions to prevent third parties from using

the Work in any way that would constitute a breach of this Agreement including, without limitation, such precautions as Sparkling would otherwise take to protect its own proprietary software or hardware or information; and
4. DELIVERY, INSTALLATION AND DATA CONVERSION

(a) In accordance with Schedule "C," Garman has delivered the required number of copies of the executable object code of the Software to those Authorized Locations (together with copies of the Documentation as is reasonably required by Sparkling to operate the Software in the manner contemplated hereunder) and installed the Software on the applicable AS400's at each Authorized Location. The installation of the Software at each existing Authorized Location shall be deemed to be completed including contracted changes and has been properly installed, is in good working order. Modifications and changes shall fall within the 60 day testing period at which time they are deemed to be completed and has been properly installed, is in good working order.

(b) For Future Installations and Conversions at an existing or new Authorized Location, Garman shall be available for Contracting required installation and conversion tasks as reasonably required, in consultation with and with the reasonable assistance of Sparkling, including conversion of Sparkling's data, as more particularly described in Schedule "D," from its current electronic form into a form suitable for processing with the Software and as required for the testing of the Software and for use of the Software as contemplated hereunder.

Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.

Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

input.quote: The parties agree that the limitation of liability in this paragraph reflects the allocation of risk between the parties and the price of the licenced Software. The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.
input.rationale: Section 15 is the only liability provision in the Agreement (Sections 11–14 contain no cap or aggregate liability language). It mutually excludes indirect and consequential damages and disapplies its limitations to Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality), but it contains no monetary cap of any kind, so each party — including Sparkling — bears unlimited exposure for direct damages. That fails the fallback, which requires a mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees. We therefore added the preferred mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000), kept the existing Section 13/14 carve-outs and extended them to indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmed that Sparkling's fee obligations are not capped "damages". The mutual exclusion of consequential damages already meets the preferred position and is left untouched.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Investigate this rule, validate any proposal, and submit one finding.

input.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Sparkling, a reasonableness standard on consent, and a bar on Garman assigning to our competitors.
input.comment: [Playbook] We added the customary carve-out allowing us to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and made consent subject to a reasonableness standard, with Garman barred from assigning to our competitors. Our playbook does not accept a blanket bar on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out; a mutual right to assign to successors on written notice is our fallback.

ops.oldText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
ops.newText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed; provided that (i) Sparkling may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or business, upon written notice to Garman, and (ii) Garman shall not assign this Agreement to any competitor of Sparkling. No change of control of Sparkling shall constitute an assignment or give Garman any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.

Category: assignment

Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.

Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

- **Auto-renewal:** none exists. Maintenance is a "renewable one-year term" (p0065), so continuation beyond 12 months requires mutual agreement and our election to pay renewal fees — the preferred position. There is no "automatically renew" language and therefore no non-renewal notice window to compute, and no multi-year renewal risk (walk-away territory avoided).
- **Exit:** the licence is perpetual while fees are paid (p0117) and we may terminate at any time on 90 days' notice (p0118), so renewals are easy for us to exit.
- **Noted, not flagged:** the Agreement/Fee Schedule contains no renewal price-uplift cap (preferred: lesser of CPI and 3%). Because it also gives Garman no unilateral escalation right, this is a missing sub-element only — worth adding if the Fee Schedule is reopened.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

**Finding submitted — deviation (LOL-CAP), Section 15 (¶p0105).**

- **Issue:** Section 15 is the Agreement's only liability provision. It mutually excludes indirect/consequential damages and disapplies its limits to Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality), but there is **no monetary cap anywhere** in the document (Sections 11–14 contain none), so both parties — including Sparkling — carry unlimited direct-damages exposure. That fails the fallback (mutual 12 months' fees cap).
- **Redline (validated, preferred level):** replaced the final sentence of ¶p0105 with a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, preserved and expanded the carve-outs (Sections 13/14, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) as uncapped "Excluded Claims", and confirmed Sparkling's fee obligations are not capped damages.
- The existing mutual consequential-damages exclusion already meets the playbook and was left untouched.

You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

Rule: LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

Preferred position:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.


Fallback position:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.


Drafter's locked target level: preferred

Original clause:
The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use. The parties agree that the limitation of liability in this paragraph reflects the allocation of risk between the parties and the price of the licenced Software. The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.

The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use. system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.

Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.

Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

**Finding submitted: deviation (GOVLAW)**

- **Clause located:** § 20(h) at paragraph p0146 — the sole governing-law/venue provision. The planner pointed to sec-20, but the operative text sits in the continuation paragraphs (p0134–p0147).
- **Issue:** Nova Scotia law and the Nova Scotia courts. Nova Scotia is outside the accepted set (New York / Delaware / California / England and Wales), so the clause fails on a material term at both the preferred and fallback level.
- **Mitigating factors noted, not flagged separately:** the venue is *non-exclusive*, so this is not full walk-away territory, and there is no arbitration clause (the only "arbitration" hit, p0090, is inside the indemnity cost definition) — so no foreign-seat problem.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** minimal substitution of the jurisdiction words only — New York law, exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County — leaving the two-sentence structure intact, per the redline guidance and the seed-govlaw precedent. The comment offers Delaware, California, or England and Wales as a fallback.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

input.quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
input.rationale: Section 20(d) imposes an absolute consent requirement on both parties with no reasonableness standard and no carve-out permitting Sparkling to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Section 3(c) reinforces this by prohibiting Sparkling from assigning except as authorized by Garman in writing. That is a blanket prohibition on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, which is walk-away territory and falls short of the fallback (mutual right to assign to successors on written notice, consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld). The document contains no change-of-control provision, so no Vendor exit or re-pricing right arises today; we added confirming language that our change of control is not an assignment. Redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out, a reasonableness standard on consent, and a bar on Garman assigning to our competitors, with a conforming cross-reference in Section 3(c).

input.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Sparkling, a reasonableness standard on consent, and a bar on Garman assigning to our competitors.
input.comment: [Playbook] We added the customary carve-out allowing us to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and made consent subject to a reasonableness standard, with Garman barred from assigning to our competitors. Our playbook does not accept a blanket bar on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out; a mutual right to assign to successors on written notice is our fallback.

input.quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
input.rationale: Section 20(d) imposes an absolute consent requirement on both parties with no reasonableness standard and no carve-out permitting Sparkling to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Section 3(c) reinforces this by prohibiting Sparkling from assigning except as authorized by Garman in writing. That is a blanket prohibition on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, which is walk-away territory and falls short of the fallback (mutual right to assign to successors on written notice, consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld). The document contains no change-of-control provision, so no Vendor exit or re-pricing right arises today; we added confirming language that our change of control is not an assignment. Redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out, a reasonableness standard on consent, and a bar on Garman assigning to our competitors, with a conforming cross-reference in Section 3(c).

paragraphs.text: 17. TERM AND TERMINATION

(a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.

(b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
(c) If either party:
(1) makes an assignment in bankruptcy or is adjudicated a bankrupt;
(2) makes a general assignment for the benefit of its creditors;

(3) has a receiver, administrator or manager of its property, assets or undertaking appointed in such circumstances as would in the reasonable discretion of the other party, detrimentally affect such other party's rights under this Agreement;
16. SOURCE CODE ESCROW
(a) Immediately upon execution of this Agreement, Garman shall maintain on each AS400 at an Authorized Location the most current version of:
(1) all source code for the Software in machine readable form, with user option to print;
(2) all program and user documentation in machine readable and printed form;

(3) all tools such as compilers, assemblers, linkers and editors required to make the source code into the functional Software operating in accordance with the Specifications as amended from time to time;

(4) a complete explanation of any procedures that are not standard practice, required to create from the source code the functional Software; (5) all documentation listing program and module inputs and their sources, outputs and their destinations, and any other relevant program and module documentation,
(collectively, the "Codes").

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.

Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.

Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.

Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

**Finding: deviation (ASSIGN, high severity)** — submitted.

**What I found**
- **§20(d) (p0142)**: "Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party." — absolute mutual consent gate, no reasonableness standard, no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out for us.
- **§3(c) (p0033)**: reinforces the bar, prohibiting Sparkling from assigning except as authorized by Garman in writing.
- **No change-of-control provision anywhere** in the document, so Garman has no CoC termination or re-pricing right today. I added confirming language rather than treating this as a separate gap.

**Why it fails the fallback**: the playbook fallback requires at minimum a mutual right to assign to successors on written notice with consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld. A blanket prohibition on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out is expressly walk-away territory — it would give Garman a veto over our own corporate transactions.

**Redline (validated ok:true, preferred position, modeled on seed-assign precedent)**
- §20(d): consent "not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed"; Sparkling may assign without consent to an affiliate or successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of substantially all assets on written notice; Garman may not assign to a Sparkling competitor; our change of control is not an assignment and triggers no Garman termination, suspension or re-pricing right.
- §3(c): conforming cross-reference "or as permitted by Section 20(d)" so the use restriction does not undercut the new carve-out.

Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. Rule: ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control

Preferred position:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Planner hints:

Check notice, frequency and cost allocation if present."}
