system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from the supplied source. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change.

This is a bounded short-document repair and you have no tools. The user supplies the exact source paragraphs, definitions, current proposal, and deterministic feedback. Return only the requested structured proposal and one-to-one element coverage. Copy every replace.oldText byte-for-byte from a supplied paragraph. Do not invent an anchor or source text.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
input.rationale: Section 17 (Term and Termination) deals only with our exit obligations (ceasing use and certifying return/destruction of Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes) and, on Garman's default, conversion to a perpetual licence plus refund of prepaid fees. There is no obligation anywhere on Garman to provide transition assistance, to return Sparkling data in a usable format, or to delete and certify deletion of our data. The only comparable provision, Section 8(b), applies solely if we exercise the Section 7 rejection option, and Section 18 survival lists no exit-assistance clause. Given Garman performs data conversion (Section 4 / Schedule "D") and holds our Confidential Information, the rule's expected clause is absent and falls short of even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export). Proposed insert adopts the preferred position (six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, deletion certification); 90 days' assistance is an acceptable fallback.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.

Category: transition

On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: missing** (medium severity) — no post-termination transition or data-return obligation on Garman.

- **Section 17** covers only term, our termination right, insolvency/default triggers, and (on Garman's default) conversion to a perpetual licence plus refund of prepaid fees. The only exit mechanics run *against us* (ceasing use and certifying return/destruction of Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes).
- **Section 8(b)** does require Garman to return our Confidential Information, but only in the narrow Section 7 rejection scenario — it is not a general exit clause.
- **Section 18** survival lists no transition or data-return provision.
- Garman performs data conversion (Section 4 / Schedule "D") and holds our Confidential Information, so the absence is material and falls short of even the fallback (90 days' assistance + 30-day export).

**Redline (validated, preferred position):** new Section 17(d) requiring Garman to provide up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return our data and Confidential Information in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, and thereafter delete and certify deletion in writing — with 90 days of assistance flagged as an acceptable fallback in the comment.

You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.

Preferred position:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.


Fallback position:

17. TERM AND TERMINATION
(b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. this Agreement may be terminated by the other party. not yet rendered.

Rule: INSURANCE — Vendor insurance

Preferred position:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.


Fallback position:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

Drafter's locked target level: preferred

Original clause:
(a) In accordance with Schedule "C," Garman has delivered the required number of copies of the executable object code of the Software to those Authorized Locations (together with copies of the Documentation as is reasonably required by Sparkling to operate the Software in the manner contemplated hereunder) and installed the Software on the applicable AS400's at each Authorized Location. The installation of the Software at each existing Authorized Location shall be deemed to be completed including contracted changes and has been properly installed, is in good working order. Modifications and changes shall fall within the 60 day testing period at which time they are deemed to be completed and has been properly installed, is in good working order.
(b) For Future Installations and Conversions at an existing or new Authorized Location, Garman shall be available for Contracting required installation and conversion tasks as reasonably required, in consultation with and with the reasonable assistance of Sparkling, including conversion of Sparkling's data, as more particularly described in Schedule "D," from its current electronic form into a form suitable for processing with the Software and as required for the testing of the Software and for use of the Software as contemplated hereunder.
(i) All paragraph headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.

Rendered redlined clause:
(a) In accordance with Schedule "C," Garman has delivered the required number of copies of the executable object code of the Software to those Authorized Locations (together with copies of the Documentation as is reasonably required by Sparkling to operate the Software in the manner contemplated hereunder) and installed the Software on the applicable AS400's at each Authorized Location. The installation of the Software at each existing Authorized Location shall be deemed to be completed including contracted changes and has been properly installed, is in good working order. Modifications and changes shall fall within the 60 day testing period at which time they are deemed to be completed and has been properly installed, is in good working order.
(b) For Future Installations and Conversions at an existing or new Authorized Location, Garman shall be available for Contracting required installation and conversion tasks as reasonably required, in consultation with and with the reasonable assistance of Sparkling, including conversion of Sparkling's data, as more particularly described in Schedule "D," from its current electronic form into a form suitable for processing with the Software and as required for the testing of the Software and for use of the Software as contemplated hereunder.
(i) All paragraph headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.
(j) Garman shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; where Garman processes, stores or has access to Sparkling's data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Garman shall provide certificates of insurance to Sparkling on request.

You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. No redline is required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-bb670a9e","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 11 FEES","rationale":"Searches for \"liquidated damages\", \"penalty\", \"interest\" and \"shall pay\" return no provision imposing liquidated damages, penalties, late-payment interest, accelerated fees or a minimum/early-termination fee on Sparkling. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Subject:** Playbook review findings, redline status and negotiation priorities

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Software License and Maintenance Agreement against the playbook and recorded 18 findings: 10 compliant, 6 deviations and 2 missing clauses. The commercial architecture is broadly favourable to us — the licence is perpetual so long as fees are paid, we hold an unqualified termination-for-convenience right on 90 days' notice, the Vendor's IP indemnity is uncapped, the Section 12 warranty exceeds our preferred 12-month position, and there is no exclusivity, non-compete, minimum commitment, MFN, auto-renewal, liquidated damages or vendor audit right anywhere in the document.

Four issues drive the negotiation. First, Section 20(d) imposes an absolute consent requirement on assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out, reinforced by Section 3(c) and by the "non-transferable" licence grant in Section 2 — we cannot move this contract to a successor. Second, Section 15 contains no monetary cap at all, so both parties bear unlimited direct-damages exposure, failing the fallback's 12-month-fees floor. Third, the Agreement is silent on Vendor insurance even though Garman installs software at our sites and converts our data. Fourth, there is no post-termination transition assistance or data return and deletion obligation on Garman. Governing law (Nova Scotia), the ownership sweep in Section 13 and the Section 19 no-hire round out the deviations.

Three of our proposed redlines did not pass verification (Licence grant scope, Transition assistance, Non-solicitation) and require manual drafting before the markup goes out. Three others were auto-repaired and should be read closely on the final pass.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (fallback) | Page 6 (§ 13) | Uncapped Vendor IP indemnity, better than the fallback super-cap; no express duty to defend, no refund remedy, 10-day notice window — noted only. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | No exclusivity, sole-supplier or minimum-requirements obligation; licence and escrow licence are non-exclusive. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No liquidated damages, penalty, late interest or exit fee; § 17 runs in our favour. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | Ordinary licence use restrictions only; § 19 is a mutual non-solicit, not a non-compete. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (fallback) | § 17 Term and Termination | § 17(b) gives us convenience termination on 90 days' notice, no exit fee; Vendor has no convenience right. No express pro-rata refund — noted. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant (better than preferred) | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No Vendor audit or usage-verification right; only inspection right (§ 16 escrow) runs in our favour. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | Page 10 (§ 20(h)) | Nova Scotia law and courts fall outside the accepted list; venue is non-exclusive, which mitigates. Proposal: New York law, exclusive New York County courts. |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 Grant of License | Perpetual and covers affiliates, but "non-transferable" with §§ 3(c)/20(d) consent gates leaves no successor path; contractors excluded. **Redline verification failed — manual drafting required.** |
| Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No MFN in either direction; an MFN in our favour is a commercial ask, not required by the rule. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Compliant | § 11 Fees | Fees payable for licence and services actually taken; maintenance is a renewable one-year term. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant (better than fallback) | § 10 Maintenance and Support | No evergreen renewal; renewal by election. No CPI/3% uplift cap, but no unilateral uplift right either — noted. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Page 9 (§ 17) | No Vendor obligation to assist on exit, return our data or certify deletion; § 8(b) applies only on § 7 rejection. **Redline verification failed — manual drafting required.** |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant (exceeds preferred) | § 12 Specifications and Warranty | Warranty for acceptance period plus one year and for the life of Maintenance Services; no "AS IS" or implied-warranty disclaimer. No services/malicious-code warranty — noted. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation (walk-away)** | Page 10 (§ 20(d)) | Blanket consent requirement, no affiliate or M&A carve-out, no reasonableness standard. Auto-repaired redline adds carve-out, reasonableness, competitor bar and change-of-control confirmation. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing (walk-away)** | Page 10 (§ 20) | No insurance covenant anywhere, yet Garman installs on-site and converts our data. Auto-repaired redline inserts preferred-position § 20(j); fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Garman ownership sweeps in "all related materials, logos, and names" and the funded Schedule "D" Modifications; no statement that we retain rights in our data. Auto-repaired redline narrows ownership, adds data ownership and a perpetual licence to funded Modifications. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | No monetary cap at all, so unlimited direct-damages exposure for us; fails the 12-month-fees fallback. Auto-repaired redline inserts mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000) with uncapped carve-outs. |
| Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees | Drafted as a no-hire covering all employees of the other party, with no advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-outs. **Redline verification failed — manual drafting required.** |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **Assignment — § 20(d) (with § 3(c)):** a blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out. We need, at minimum, the fallback: a mutual right to assign to a successor on written notice, with consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld.
2. **Vendor insurance — § 20 (absent):** a vendor that works on our premises and processes our data carries no insurance obligation at all. Preferred position inserted as new § 20(j); E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is the acceptable fallback.
3. **Non-solicitation — § 19:** a no-hire covering all of the other party's employees. We need conversion to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.

We also treat the absence of any liability cap in § 15 as a priority ask, since the unlimited exposure runs against us as well as Garman.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Manual drafting (before markup issues):** prepare redlines for LICENSE (§ 2 — contractors and successor transfer), TRANSITION (new § 17 exit assistance, machine-readable data return within 30 days, deletion certification; 90 days' assistance is an acceptable fallback) and NOSOLICIT (§ 19 rewrite). The automated proposals for these three did not verify.
2. **Quality-check the auto-repaired redlines** for ASSIGN, INSURANCE, IP and LOL-CAP against the section text before circulation.
3. **Send the markup with the four priority asks front-loaded:** assignment carve-out, § 15 mutual cap, § 20(j) insurance, § 19 non-solicit; then governing law (New York, exclusive New York County courts), the § 13 ownership narrowing and the § 2 transfer right.
4. **Raise conversationally, not by redline:** express duty to defend and a longer indemnity notice window (§ 13); 30 days' notice and an express pro-rata refund on convenience termination (§ 17(b)); a CPI/3% cap on renewal maintenance fees if the Fee Schedule is reopened; a services, malicious-code and compliance-with-laws warranty (§ 12); and, as a commercial ask only, an MFN in our favour.
5. **Hold the line on current advantages:** resist any Vendor attempt to introduce an audit or usage-verification right (and if one is introduced, insist on once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, vendor cost, no system access), and preserve the mutual exclusion of consequential damages and the § 13/§ 14 carve-outs as drafted.
6. **Escalate to the business** if Garman refuses any of the three walk-away items, so that the sponsor can weigh signature risk before we trade elsewhere."}

## 3. Walk-away items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **Assignment — § 20(d) (with § 3(c)):** a blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out. We need, at minimum, the fallback: a mutual right to assign to a successor on written notice, with consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld.
2. **Vendor insurance — § 20 (absent):** a vendor that works on our premises and processes our data carries no insurance obligation at all. Preferred position inserted as new § 20(j); E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is the acceptable fallback.
3. **Non-solicitation — § 19:** a no-hire covering all of the other party's employees. We need conversion to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.

We also treat the absence of any liability cap in § 15 as a priority ask, since the unlimited exposure runs against us as well as Garman.
